key_insight: A parameter-regularised Ensemble Kalman Filter can sequentially tune RANS turbulence-model parameters on a simple urban case and transfer them to more complex city flows while keeping updates physically plausible.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to improve urban wind, ventilation, and pollutant-dispersion simulations with less manual calibration and better robustness across different building configurations.
method: Derive a PR-EnKF for sequential Bayesian parameter estimation in RANS turbulence models
Regularize updates with prior knowledge to keep parameters in physical ranges
Train on an isolated building, then transfer parameters to higher-rise, multi-building, and district-scale cases
evidence_signal: The abstract reports faster convergence, about an order-of-magnitude reduction in parameter uncertainty, and reconstruction errors reduced by up to 50% across the transfer tests.
watch_item: Transferability still depends on the quality of the prior and the similarity between training and target urban flow regimes, so poor priors or strongly different physics may limit performance.
paper_title: Transferable inference of turbulence models for urban flows with the Parameter-Regularised Ensemble Kalman Filter
